gap: Perplexity Sonar Pro — AI-synthesized answer provider (search-cli, pi-websearch, last30days-skill)
effort_estimate: 1-2 days (new backend, Perplexity API is OpenAI-compatible)
notes: Returns synthesized answers rather than raw results — useful for quick agent queries but breaks the raw-retrieval paradigm. Add as optional backend only.

gap: Serper (Google SERP) — direct Google search results page provider (search-cli, pi-websearch)
notes: Cost leader at ~$0.30/1K queries. Valuable for price-sensitive users. Google freshness is often superior to Brave/Tavily for trending topics.

gap: SerpAPI — 40+ search engines via one provider (search-cli, pi-websearch)
notes: Overlap with Serper for basic Google. Unique value is Yahoo, Yandex, eBay, etc. — fringe value for English-language agent search.

gap: Firecrawl — JS-rendered web page scraping / crawling (search-cli, pi-websearch, ketch)
effort_estimate: 2-3 days (two use cases: scrape single URL + crawl site)
notes: Overlaps with Jina reader (which asearch has). Firecrawl is stronger for JS-heavy SPAs. Could be added as alternative reader backend.

gap: Browserless / Stealth scraper — cloud browser rendering, anti-bot scraping (search-cli)
notes: Powerful but niche. Useful for scraping sites that block conventional scrapers. Low priority unless users specifically request blocked-site support.

gap: Parallel AI, Linkup, Valyu, You.com — alternative search API providers (pi-websearch)
effort_estimate: 1-2 days each (all are simple REST APIs)
notes: Parallel is slowest (13.6s latency). Valyu and You.com are smaller players. Linkup has interesting agent-native design. Low urgency, moderate value for fallback diversity.

gap: xAI/Grok — X/Twitter search via Grok API (search-cli)
notes: X/Twitter is already supported via twitter-cli. Grok API may provide better X search but requires separate subscription. Low priority.

gap: Code search — grep.app, Sourcegraph, GitHub code search backends (ketch)
effort_estimate: 3-5 days (3 backends + language filter + regex support)
notes: **Highest-value missing source.** ketch's code search is its moat and directly relevant to asearch's target audience (coding agents). grep.app is free and needs no API key. Sourcegraph and GitHub code search are well-documented. This is the #1 gap to close.

gap: Library/docs search — Context7 version-aware doc snippets (ketch)
notes: Valuable for coding agents that need framework/library documentation. Could be paired with code search launch.

gap: Chinese social platforms — Bilibili, Zhihu, Xiaohongshu, Douyin, Weibo, WeChat, V2EX, Xueqiu (Agent-Reach, AutoCLI)
effort_estimate: 4-6 weeks (massive scope, requires CLI tools + auth per platform)
notes: Huge effort for marginal return outside Chinese market. Agent-Reach requires per-platform CLI tools and cookie auth. Only pursue if asearch gains Chinese user base.

gap: TikTok — short-form video captions/comments (last30days-skill, AutoCLI)
notes: Growing relevance for trend analysis. last30days-skill proves it's doable. Moderate value.

gap: Instagram Reels/Posts — Meta platform content (last30days-skill, AutoCLI)
notes: Limited API access. Niche use cases (brand monitoring, influencer research). Low priority.

gap: LinkedIn — professional network data (AutoCLI, Agent-Reach)
effort_estimate: 2-3 days (scraper tool-based, similar to Agent-Reach approach)
notes: Valuable for B2B research and recruiting use cases. Moderate effort, moderate value.

gap: Polymarket — prediction market data (last30days-skill)
notes: Interesting niche for serious investors/researchers. Low effort to add, narrow appeal.

gap: YouTube transcripts — full video transcription beyond just metadata (last30days-skill, Agent-Reach via yt-dlp)
notes: asearch already supports YouTube via yt-dlp for metadata. Transcript extraction adds significant value for research/deep dives. YouTube is already listed as a 🔧 dependency — leverage it further.

gap: Reddit comments — threaded comment data beyond just posts (last30days-skill, AutoCLI)
effort_estimate: 1-2 days (extend existing Reddit source to fetch comments via /r/sub/comments/id.json)
notes: asearch already has Reddit source. Adding comment fetching is natural extension. High value for sentiment/discussion analysis.

gap: RSS/Atom feeds — feed-based content consumption (Agent-Reach)
notes: Useful for monitoring blogs and news sites. Could be implemented via a generic feed reader backend.

gap: Arxiv — academic paper search (AutoCLI)
notes: Valuable for research-oriented agents. Low effort, moderate value. Could pair with code search launch.

gap: Wikipedia — encyclopedia content (AutoCLI)
notes: Low effort, moderate value for factual grounding. Many agents use Wikipedia as reliable baseline.

gap: Podcast/audio content — Apple Podcasts, Xiaoyuzhou via Whisper transcription (AutoCLI, Agent-Reach)
notes: Interesting but heavy. Whisper transcription is resource-intensive. Niche appeal.

gap: Bluesky, Threads, Digg — emerging social platforms (last30days-skill)
notes: Bluesky is gaining traction. Threads has no API. Digg is AI-focused. Low priority but Bluesky could become relevant.

gap: Intent-specific search modes — academic, people, scholar, patents, images, places, deep, social (search-cli)
effort_estimate: 3-5 days (depends on provider support — Serper/SerpAPI have specialized endpoints)
notes: search-cli has 14 modes. Many map to Serper/SerpAPI special endpoints. Without those providers, modes are limited. Could implement subset via existing providers (e.g., 'news' mode via Brave/Tavily).

gap: Streaming results — results appear as providers respond (search-cli)
notes: Improves perceived performance. search-cli streams via tokio::JoinSet. Would require architectural change to asearch's parallel fetch → collect → return model.

gap: Self-update command — `asearch update` pulls latest binary (search-cli)
notes: Standard UX improvement. Low effort. asearch already has version command and npm wrapper. Self-update for Go binary downloaders would be nice.

gap: Config file with subcommands — `asearch config set/get/show/check` (search-cli, ketch)
notes: Currently asearch uses only env vars. Config file would enable persistent defaults and per-key settings. ketch has ~/.config/ketch/config.json. search-cli uses TOML. Valuable for session defaults, preferred source ordering, etc.

gap: Auto-JSON detection — automatically output JSON when piped (search-cli)
notes: **Critical UX gap for agent usage.** Agents frequently pipe output. Currently asearch requires explicit --json flag or --raw mode. Auto-detection would make piped workflows seamless. Very low effort.

gap: Semantic exit codes — 4 categories of exit codes for different outcomes (search-cli)
notes: Enables better agent error handling (distinguish 'no results' from 'API error' from 'timeout'). search-cli has 4 categories. Valuable for production agent workflows.

gap: Shell completion generation — `asearch completion bash|zsh|fish` (AutoCLI, ketch, search-cli)
effort_estimate: 1 day (cobra supports this natively in Go)
notes: Since asearch uses cobra (based on commands), shell completion is likely straightforward. Improves developer UX for interactive use.

gap: Multiple output formats — table, JSON, YAML, CSV, Markdown (AutoCLI, ketch)
notes: Currently asearch has JSON, raw, and terminal table. CSV and Markdown would be useful for data export. Moderate value.

gap: URL scraping for clean markdown — `asearch scrape <url>` extracts readable content (ketch)
effort_estimate: 1-2 days (Jina reader API is already available; add direct URL scrape command)
notes: **High-frequency agent workflow**: agent finds URLs via search, then wants to read them. ketch has `--scrape` flag. asearch could use Jina reader (already integrated) or direct HTTP fetch with readability. This is a key gap — agents need to read pages, not just find them.

gap: Website crawling — BFS/sitemap-based site-wide content extraction (ketch)
notes: Valuable for documentation scraping and site auditing. ketch has background crawl with status tracking. Significant effort but high standalone value.

gap: Background crawl execution with status tracking — list/status/stop (ketch)
notes: Heavy feature. ketch's crawl system is sophisticated. Only useful if asearch adds crawling. Low priority.

gap: Page cache with configurable TTL — avoids refetching same URLs (ketch)
notes: Performance optimization. ketch caches scraped pages for 72h by default. Valuable for repeated queries on same topics. asearch already has ~/.asearch storage — natural extension.

gap: CSS selector extraction — extract specific elements from pages (ketch)
notes: Power-user feature for targeted data extraction. Low effort, low general appeal.

gap: Browser rendering for JS-rendered pages (ketch via headless Chrome, search-cli via Firecrawl)
notes: Requires Chrome installation or Firecrawl API key. Niche but valuable for scraping modern SPAs.

gap: /llms.txt detection — auto-discover site's LLM optimization file (ketch)
notes: Trending convention. Sites are adding llms.txt to guide AI consumption. Low effort, signal of modernity.

gap: Auto-detect router that probes available API keys in priority order (pi-websearch)
notes: **Major UX improvement.** Currently asearch has hardcoded Tavily→Exa→Brave→SearXNG fallback. pi-websearch's resolveProvider() dynamically probes available keys. Would make key management seamless. High value.

gap: Provider-specific parameters — e.g., Exa date filter, Brave freshness, domain include/exclude (pi-websearch, search-cli)
notes: Power-user feature. search-cli has per-provider timeouts. pi-websearch passes provider-specific params through tool schemas. Valuable but adds CLI complexity.

gap: AI-driven narrative synthesis — auto-generate summaries/briefs from search results (last30days-skill)
effort_estimate: 3-5 days (LLM integration, prompt engineering, output rendering)
notes: last30days-skill's signature feature. Would require LLM API key as optional dependency. Valuable but shifts asearch's focus from 'search tool' to 'research assistant'.

gap: Shareable HTML briefs — publication-ready offline artifacts (last30days-skill)
notes: Useful for sharing research results. last30days-skill generates dark-mode HTML files. Moderate effort, moderate value.

gap: Entity resolution / pre-research — auto-discover handles, subreddits, hashtags before search (last30days-skill)
notes: Sophisticated feature from last30days-skill. AI-powered pre-search phase. Over-engineered for most use cases.

gap: Trend monitoring with persistence — SQLite-backed watchlist with scheduled briefings (last30days-skill)
effort_estimate: 5-10 days (SQLite schema, cron scheduling, briefing generation)
notes: Major feature. Shifts asearch from CLI tool to daemon/service. Interesting but scope expansion.

gap: Engagement-based scoring / humor scoring — rank results by social engagement (last30days-skill)
notes: Novel feature from last30days-skill. Adds personality but complex to implement well. Not essential.

gap: MCP server — expose asearch as Model Context Protocol server (Agent-Reach, general industry trend)
effort_estimate: 3-5 days (MCP protocol implementation in Go, tool definitions)
notes: **High industry demand.** MCP is becoming the standard for LLM-tool integration. Agent-Reach has MCP integration. Exposing asearch as an MCP server would dramatically increase adoption in the AI agent ecosystem.

gap: Cookie-based auth for blocked platforms (Agent-Reach)
effort_estimate: 2-3 days (cookie file import + HTTP client configuration)
notes: Useful for scraping rate-limited or login-walled sites. Low priority unless users request specific blocked sources.

gap: Multi-language UI / i18n support (Agent-Reach)
notes: Agent-Reach supports Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean. asearch currently has Russian/English. Valuable if pursuing international users.

gap: AI-powered adapter generation — `asearch explore` discovers and generates new source adapters (AutoCLI)
notes: AutoCLI's most ambitious feature. AI generates YAML adapters for new sites. Very complex, niche appeal.

gap: YAML pipeline definitions — declarative custom workflows (AutoCLI)
effort_estimate: 5-10 days (pipeline interpreter, step execution, expression engine)
notes: Powerful but massive scope. Would make asearch a general-purpose scraping framework. Not recommended.

gap: Write operations — post, reply, like, follow on social platforms (AutoCLI)
notes: AutoCLI can write to social media. This is a fundamentally different product direction from asearch's read-only search focus.

gap: Desktop app control — control Cursor, Codex, ChatGPT, Notion, Discord (AutoCLI)
notes: Interesting but well outside asearch's scope. AutoCLI uses Chrome extension for desktop control.

gap: External CLI passthrough — run `asearch gh issue list` wrapping `gh` (AutoCLI)
notes: Neat but blurs product boundaries. asearch should focus on search, not generic CLI passthrough.

gap: Homebrew formula — `brew install agent-asearch` for macOS users (ketch, search-cli)
notes: **Significant adoption blocker.** macOS users expect `brew install`. ketch and search-cli both have Homebrew. Currently only npm install and manual binary download. High impact, low effort.

gap: Regex-based intent classification — auto-detect search intent from query (search-cli)
notes: search-cli classifies queries to select best provider/source. Could improve asearch's default source selection. Moderate value.

gap: Per-provider timeout and retry configuration (search-cli)
effort_estimate: 1-2 days (configurable timeout per backend, retry policy)
notes: search-cli has per-provider timeouts using tokio::JoinSet. Improves resilience when one provider is slow. Moderate value for production reliability.

gap: URL dedup with normalization across providers (search-cli)
notes: **Important quality improvement.** When searching multiple providers, the same result often appears. search-cli deduplicates by normalized URL. Helps reduce token waste in LLM contexts. Low effort.

gap: Provider fallback chain — try providers in priority order with automatic fallback (search-cli's steal→jina→firecrawl→browserless model)
effort_estimate: 2-3 days (fallback mechanism + health check per provider)
notes: **Critical reliability improvement.** search-cli's 'steal' mode tries 4 providers in sequence with fallback. asearch currently has basic auto-delegation but no structured fallback with timeouts. Would make searches more reliable.

gap: Modular package-per-provider architecture (pi-websearch)
effort_estimate: 3-5 days (extract each backend into separate package/module, core interface)
notes: pi-websearch has monorepo with core + individual provider packages. Improves maintainability and enables third-party provider packages. Low immediate user value but good engineering practice.

gap: Compile-time embedded adapters — sources compiled into binary, zero runtime discovery (AutoCLI, ketch)
notes: asearch already compiles sources into Go binary. No gap here — this is an asearch strength inherited from Go's static compilation.

gap: Page cache with TTL and configurable expiry (ketch)
notes: ketch caches scraped pages for 72h by default. asearch already stores sessions locally — adding page caching is natural extension. Reduces API costs and improves latency.

gap: Background/async execution with job tracking (ketch)
effort_estimate: 5-7 days (job manager, PID tracking, status reporting)
notes: ketch runs crawls in background with list/status/stop commands. Heavy feature. Only relevant if asearch adds crawling.

gap: Pluggable AI post-processing pipeline — entity resolution, synthesis, scoring as modular stages (last30days-skill)
effort_estimate: 5-10 days (pipeline architecture, stage interface, LLM integration)
notes: Sophisticated architecture. last30days-skill chains search → entity resolution → scoring → synthesis → briefing. Valuable but shifts product scope toward full research assistant.

gap: Colored terminal table output — human-readable colored results (search-cli)
notes: Improves interactive CLI experience. asearch currently has terminal output but without color. Low effort, noticeable polish improvement.

gap: Streaming result display — results appear as they arrive (search-cli)
notes: Better perceived performance. search-cli shows results progressively. asearch currently waits for all providers then returns. Moderate effort.

gap: Auto-JSON mode when piped (search-cli)
notes: **Critical for agent workflows.** When piped to jq or another command, auto-switch to JSON. Currently requires explicit flag. Very low effort, very high impact.

gap: Shell completion (AutoCLI, ketch)
notes: Low effort, noticeable polish for interactive users.

gap: --dry-run mode — show what would be searched without executing (Agent-Reach)
notes: Useful for debugging. Agent-Reach has --dry-run install mode. Demonstrates which sources/keys would be used.

gap: --safe mode — strict/read-only operations (Agent-Reach)
effort_estimate: 1 day (safe mode flag, restrict to read-only operations)
notes: Good for CI/CD and production agent use. Prevents accidental destructive operations.

gap: Multi-format output — --format json|yaml|csv|md|table (AutoCLI, ketch)
notes: Improves interoperability with different workflows. AutoCLI has 5 output formats. Moderate value.

gap: Progress/spinner during search execution (ketch, search-cli)
notes: Polishes interactive experience. Shows which sources are being queried. Low effort.

gap: Config file management — `config set default-source hn` (ketch, search-cli)
notes: Enables persistent user preferences. ketch has `ketch config set/get/init`. Low effort, high convenience value.

gap: ELI5 / plain language rewrite mode (last30days-skill)
notes: Charming feature from last30days-skill. Low effort with LLM integration. Niche but delightful.

gap: Provider-aware help text — `asearch help sources` shows available + configured sources (search-cli's agent-info command)
effort_estimate: 1 day (dynamic help generation based on env/keys)
notes: search-cli's `agent-info` command shows configured providers. asearch's `doctor` partially does this but could show richer status.
